一个普通员工每月毛工资约 4,850 欧元。

06

01

According to the Federal Statistical Office, a full-time employee in Germany earns about 4,850 euros gross per month on average.

据联邦统计局，德国全职员工平均毛月薪约 4,850 欧元。

02

That is the average; the median is much lower, because top earners pull the average up.

这是平均数；中位数低得多，因为高收入者拉高了平均值。

03

Taxes and social contributions are deducted from the gross salary.

税和社保从毛工资中扣除。

04

In 2026, the employee's social contributions total about 21 percent.

2026 年，雇员社保合计约 21%。

05

This includes pensions (9.3%), health insurance (7.3% plus a supplement), care insurance (1.7-2.4%) and unemployment insurance (1.3%).

包括养老（9.3%）、医保（7.3% 加附加费）、护理（1.7–2.4%）和失业险（1.3%）。

06

At a gross salary of 4,850 euros, about 3,053 euros remain net - roughly 37 percent in deductions.

毛工资 4,850 欧元时，到手约 3,053 欧元——扣除约 37%。

07

In 2026 you pay no income tax on the first 12,084 euros a year (basic allowance).

2026 年，年收入前 12,084 欧元（基本免税额）不缴所得税。

08

About 90 percent of taxpayers no longer pay the solidarity surcharge.

约 90% 的纳税人不再缴团结附加税。

毛工资中扣除所得税和社保；2026 年雇员的社保份额约 21%。

01

Many companies in Germany offer their employees a bicycle.

德国很多公司给员工提供自行车。

02

It is called a Dienstrad or Jobrad.

这叫作 Dienstrad 或 JobRad。

03

The company leases the bike and the employee pays part of the salary for it.

公司租下这辆车，员工用一部分工资来付。

04

The money is taken from the gross salary, so the employee pays less tax.

这笔钱从税前工资扣除，所以员工少缴税。

05

The contract usually lasts three years.

合同通常持续三年。

06

After that, the employee can often buy the bike at a leftover price.

之后员工通常可以按残值买下这辆车。

07

In 2025, about 342,000 companies offered this benefit.

2025 年约有 34.2 万家公司提供这项福利。

08

About 22.6 million employees were eligible, but only about 2.4 million used it.

B1 B1 · 完整句子，加了连接词和从句
🎧 听这一版
01

More and more employers in Germany offer company bike leasing.

德国越来越多的雇主提供公司自行车租赁。

02

According to a study by Deloitte and Zukunft Fahrrad, around 342,000 companies offered it in 2025 - about 20 percent more than the year before.

据 Deloitte 与 Zukunft Fahrrad 的研究，2025 年约有 34.2 万家公司提供，比前一年多约 20%。

03

About 22.6 million employees had access, roughly half of the workforce.

约 2260 万雇员有资格，约占劳动力的一半。

04

Only about 2.4 million actually used the offer, around 11 percent of those eligible.

实际使用只有约 240 万，约占合格者的 11%。

05

There are two common models: the employer provides the bike on top of the salary, which is tax-free until the end of 2030, or employees pay the lease rate through a salary conversion.

常见两种模式：公司额外配车，免税到 2030 年底；或员工通过工资转化支付月供。

06

With salary conversion, private use is taxed at 0.25 percent of the list price per month, far less than a company car.

工资转化模式下，私人使用按标价每月 0.25% 缴税，远低于公司汽车。

07

After the usual three-year term, employees can often buy the bike at its residual value.

在通常三年的合同结束后，员工通常可以按残值买下。

08

JobRad, the market leader, says it works with more than 100,000 employers and about seven million eligible employees.

市场龙头 JobRad 称覆盖 10 万多家雇主、约 700 万合格雇员。

03 / 05
B2 B2 · 书面表达（被动、分词短语、名词化）
🎧 听这一版
01

According to the latest Deloitte study, around 342,000 companies offered bike leasing in 2025, 20 percent more than in 2024.

据最新 Deloitte 研究，2025 年约有 34.2 万家公司提供租车，比 2024 年多 20%。

02

About 22.6 million employees had access, but only about 2.4 million used the offer - roughly 11 percent of those eligible.

约 2260 万雇员有资格，但只有约 240 万使用——约占合格者的 11%。

03

Market revenue was 2.8 billion euros in 2025, down four percent, with around 720,000 newly leased bikes.

2025 年市场营收 28 亿欧元，下降 4%，新租出约 72 万辆。

04

If the employer provides the bike on top of the salary, private use is tax-free under § 3 No. 37 EStG until 31 December 2030.

若公司在工资之外额外配车，私人使用依据《所得税法》第 3 条第 37 款免税至 2030 年 12 月 31 日。

05

With salary conversion, private use is taxed under the 0.25 percent rule: one quarter of the list price, rounded down to full 100 euros, at one percent per month.

工资转化模式下，私人使用按 0.25% 规则缴税：标价的四分之一（取整到整百欧），每月按 1% 计。

06

For an e-bike with a list price of 4,000 euros, that is ten euros of taxable benefit per month.

以标价 4,000 欧的 E-Bike 为例，每月应税收益为 10 欧。

07

After three years, tax authorities generally accept 40 percent of the rounded list price as the residual value for a buyout.

三年后，税务部门通常认可取整标价的 40% 作为买断残值。

08

JobRad holds around 45 percent of the market and reached two million leased bikes in 2025, about 80 percent of them e-bikes.

JobRad 占约 45% 的市场份额，2025 年累计租出 200 万辆，其中约 80% 是 E-Bike。

01

In Germany, people with sudden health problems often call the emergency number and are taken to a hospital emergency department by ambulance.

在德国，突然出现健康问题的人常常打急救电话，并由救护车送到医院急诊室。

02

Experts point out that many of these cases are not real emergencies and put pressure on hospitals.

专家指出，很多这类情况并非真正的急症，却给医院带来压力。

03

The Bundestag has passed a reform of emergency care.

04

Under the new law, an expert will first check whether the patient's life is in danger.

根据新法律，专家会先检查病人的生命是否有危险。

05

The check can take place by phone or on site.

这项检查可以在电话里或现场进行。

06

Patients who do not need emergency care can be sent to a doctor's practice.

不需要急诊的病人可以被转到诊所。

07

New emergency centres will decide which doctor a patient needs.

新的急诊中心将决定病人需要哪位医生。

08

The aim is to reduce the number of people in emergency departments and to help patients faster.

目标是减少急诊室的人数，并更快地帮助病人。

01

People in Germany who suddenly fall ill often call the emergency number and are taken to hospital by ambulance.

在德国，突然生病的人常常打急救电话，并被救护车送到医院。

02

However, experts note that a considerable number of these cases are not medically necessary and are therefore expensive.

然而专家指出，其中相当一部分情况在医学上并无必要，因而费用高昂。

03

For this reason, the Bundestag has passed a reform of emergency care aimed at directing patients more effectively.

因此，联邦议院通过了急诊医疗改革，旨在更有效地引导病人。

04

In future, an expert is to assess first whether there is a real threat to life, either by phone or on site.

今后，专家应先评估是否真的存在生命危险，可以在电话里或现场进行。

05

Patients without an acute emergency can be referred to a doctor's practice, while those in critical condition continue to go directly to an emergency department.

没有急性急症的病人可以被转到诊所，而情况危急的病人仍然直接去急诊室。

06

Integrated emergency centres are also intended to determine which specialist treatment is required.

整合急诊中心还将确定需要哪种专业治疗。

07

The reform is meant to relieve overcrowded emergency departments and shorten waiting times.

这项改革旨在减轻拥挤的急诊室负担，并缩短等待时间。

08

The law still has to be approved by the Bundesrat before it can take effect.

该法律在生效前还必须得到联邦参议院的批准。

01

Jürgen Linnemann, 57, has spent roughly 40 years in workshops for people with disabilities and currently digitalises documents three days a week in Freckenhorst, North Rhine-Westphalia.

57 岁的尤尔根·林内曼在残障人士工坊工作了约 40 年，目前在弗雷肯霍斯特每周三天把文件数字化。

02

For about 24 hours of work a week he receives just under 200 euros a month — roughly two euros per hour.

每周约 24 小时的工作，他每月拿到不到 200 欧——约合每小时 2 欧。

03

The statutory minimum wage has stood at 13.90 euros gross per hour since January 2026, but it does not currently apply to workshop employees.

法定最低工资自 2026 年 1 月起为每小时 13,90 欧（税前），但目前不适用于工坊员工。

04

Under German law, they are not regarded as employees in the sense of the Minimum Wage Act; instead they receive a workshop allowance under § 221 of the Social Code.

根据德国法律，他们不被视为《最低工资法》意义上的雇员，而是按《社会法典》第 221 条领取工坊报酬。

05

Linnemann considers this unequal treatment unfair and has sued his employer for the minimum wage.

林内曼认为这种不平等待遇不公平，并起诉雇主支付最低工资。

06

The workshop says that paying the minimum wage to all of its roughly 1,300 employees would not be financially feasible.

工坊表示，给约 1300 名员工全部支付最低工资在财务上无法承受。

07

The labour court in Münster postponed its ruling; a decision is expected in November or December.

明斯特劳动法院推迟了裁决；判决预计在 11 月或 12 月作出。

08

With around 300,000 people employed in some 700 workshops across Germany, the case is seen as a test case of national significance.

由于德国约有 30 万人在约 700 家工坊就业，此案被视为具有全国意义的示范性诉讼。

When the children are 65, they get the money.

01

Four weeks after the Berlin election, Linke, Grüne and SPD finished their exploratory talks.

柏林选举四周后，左翼党、绿党和社民党结束了试探性谈判。

02

They agreed to socialise large private housing companies that own more than 10,000 flats in Berlin.

他们同意把在柏林拥有超过 1 万套住房的大型私营住房公司收归公有。

03

Companies may keep 10,000 flats; the rest would go to the state of Berlin in return for compensation.

04

About five companies, including Vonovia, and around 160,000 flats would be affected.

约 5 家公司（包括 Vonovia）和约 16 万套住房会受影响。

05

Compensation would be limited to 16 billion euros.

补偿将被限制在 160 亿欧元以内。

06

Cooperatives and buildings completed after 1 January 2021 are exempt.

合作社和 2021 年 1 月 1 日以后建成的住房除外。

07

A law is planned for mid-2028 and would take effect one year after it is passed.

法案计划于 2028 年中期出台，并在通过一年后生效。

08

The CDU and the federal building ministry criticise the plan.

基民盟和联邦建设部批评这个计划。

01

After finishing exploratory talks, Linke, Grüne and SPD want to start coalition negotiations in Berlin.

结束试探性谈判后，柏林左翼党、绿党和社民党希望启动联合政府谈判。

02

The core of the agreement is the socialisation of private housing companies that own more than 10,000 flats in the city.

协议的核心是把在柏林拥有超过 1 万套住房的私营住房公司收归公有。

03

Companies would keep a base stock of 10,000 flats; the rest would become the property of the state of Berlin against compensation.

企业将保留 1 万套的基本存量；其余部分在获得补偿后成为柏林州的财产。

04

According to Linke figures, five major companies – including Vonovia – and around 160,000 flats would be affected, with compensation capped at 16 billion euros.

据左翼党方面数据，5 家大公司（包括 Vonovia）和约 16 万套住房将受影响，补偿上限为 160 亿欧元。

05

Cooperatives, public-interest actors and flats built after 1 January 2021 are excluded.

合作社、公共利益机构以及 2021 年 1 月 1 日以后建成的住房不在其中。

06

The legal basis would be Article 15 of the Basic Law, which has never been applied before.

法律依据将是《基本法》第 15 条，该条此前从未被适用。

07

The law is expected in mid-2028 and would enter into force one year after its passage, subject to constitutional review.

该法预计于 2028 年中期出台，并在通过一年后生效，届时须经合宪性审查。

08

While the federal building ministry has announced a law against socialisation, the Berlin parties will now let their committees decide on coalition talks.

联邦建设部已宣布要推出一项反收归公有的法律，而柏林三党现在将让各自机构决定是否启动联合政府谈判。

01

When a person's heart stops beating, their life is in danger.

一个人的心脏停止跳动时，生命就有危险。

02

People can restart the heart by pressing hard on the chest.

人们可以通过用力按压胸廓让心脏重新跳动。

03

This is called resuscitation, or CPR.

这叫做心肺复苏。

04

They must also blow air into the person's mouth.

还必须往这个人的嘴里吹气。

05

Many people are afraid to do it because they think they will make a mistake.

很多人不敢做，因为他们觉得自己会弄错。

06

On World Restart a Heart Day, people in Germany can practise.

在世界重启心脏日，德国人可以练习。

07

Doctors and paramedics show how it works on a dummy.

医生和急救人员用假人示范怎么做。

01

A cardiac arrest is life-threatening: if the heart stops, a person dies without help.

心脏骤停危及生命：心脏一旦停跳，得不到帮助的人就会死亡。

02

During CPR, the chest is pressed down again and again so that the heart is massaged.

做心肺复苏时，要反复向下按压胸廓，让心脏受到按摩。

03

Often the heart starts beating again.

心脏往往又会开始跳动。

04

Air is also blown into the person's mouth.

同时还要向这个人的嘴里吹气。

05

Many people do not dare to perform chest compressions because they are afraid of making mistakes.

很多人不敢做胸外按压，因为他们害怕弄错。

06

On World Restart a Heart Day, hospitals in Germany offered training sessions.

世界重启心脏日当天，德国的医院举办了培训活动。

07

Medical staff and paramedics demonstrated the correct technique on dummies.

医护人员和急救人员在假人上示范了正确的技术。

01

Cardiac arrest is acutely life-threatening; without rapid help, the person will die.

心脏骤停会急性危及生命；得不到及时帮助，人就会死亡。

02

Chest compressions, performed rhythmically on the ribcage, can often restore a heartbeat.

有节奏地按压胸廓，常常能让心脏恢复跳动。

03

In addition, rescue breaths are given by blowing air into the person's mouth.

此外，还要通过向患者口中吹气进行人工呼吸。

04

Many people hesitate because they worry about doing something wrong.

许多人犹豫，是因为担心自己做错。

05

On World Restart a Heart Day, people across Germany had the chance to practise chest compressions.

01

On 20 October 2026 the European Parliament voted to strengthen passenger rights across the EU.

2026 年 10 月 20 日，欧盟议会投票决定加强全欧盟的乘客权利。

02

The vote was clear: 652 members voted in favour and only two against.

表决结果明确：652 票赞成，仅两票反对。

03

Travellers who book through an online platform will also get the booking fee back if their trip is cancelled.

通过在线平台订票的旅客，在行程取消时也能拿回订票费。

04

Refunds must reach the passenger within 14 days.

05

将有一个统一投诉表格，提供全部欧盟官方语言版本。

06

National authorities will be able to start investigations on their own.

各国主管机关将可以主动启动调查。

在生效之前，欧盟理事会仍须批准该协议。

01

The reform adopted on 20 October 2026 aims to make passenger rights easier to enforce across the EU.

2026 年 10 月 20 日通过的这项改革，旨在让乘客权利在欧盟范围内更容易落实。

02

Where a trip is booked through an intermediary such as a travel agency or an online platform, the refund is to include the intermediary's fee.

如果行程是通过旅行社或网络平台等中介预订的，退款应包含中介费。

03

The refund must reach the traveller within 14 days: the operator transfers the money to the intermediary within seven days, which then has another seven days to pass it on.

退款须在 14 天内到达旅客手中：运营方须在七天内把钱转给中介，中介再在七天内转交旅客。

04

A uniform claim form, provided by the Commission in all official languages, is meant to make refund and compensation requests simpler.

由欧盟委员会以所有官方语言提供的统一申请表格，应能简化退款与赔偿申请。

05

Companions of passengers with reduced mobility may fly free of charge where their presence is required for safety reasons.

行动不便乘客的陪同人员，在出于安全原因必须同行的情况下可以免费乘机。

06

National authorities gain wider powers and may launch audits and investigations without waiting for a complaint.

各国主管机关获得更大权限，无需等待投诉即可发起审计和调查。

07

Most provisions are due to apply from 23 October 2027, after the Council of the EU formally confirms the agreement.

多数条款应从 2027 年 10 月 23 日起适用，此前欧盟理事会须正式确认该协议。

🎧 听这一版
01

The Forsa survey for the Studienkreis (2,002 parents, May–June 2024) puts paid tutoring from Year 5 at 19 percent.

Studienkreis 委托的 Forsa 调查（2.002 位家长，2024 年 5–6 月）显示，五年级以上付费补习比例为 19%。

02

In the upper secondary years the figure is 17 percent; overall, 22 percent of parents have paid for tutoring at least once.

高中阶段为 17%；总体上，22% 的家长至少付过一次补课费。

03

Tutoring concentrates on maths, German and English and is often short-term.

补课集中在数学、德语和英语，且常常是短期的。

04

Comparability is limited: depending on the survey, figures range from 6 to 27 percent.

可比性有限：不同调查的数值从 6% 到 27% 不等。

05

The link to family background is striking: 25 percent of parents with a lower secondary certificate paid for tutoring, compared with 19 percent of parents with the Abitur.

与家庭背景的关联很显眼：25% 的低学历家长付过补课费，而 Abitur 学历家长为 19%。

06

Tutoring therefore responds to gaps and transitions rather than simply replacing classroom teaching.

因此，补课是对知识缺口和升学过渡的反应，而不是简单替代课堂教学。

07

Under the Ganztagsförderungsgesetz, all-day primary care becomes a legal entitlement from 2026/27, starting with Year 1 and covering all four years by 2029/30.

根据《全日促进法》，小学全日看护从 2026/27 起成为法定权利，从一年级开始，到 2029/30 覆盖全部四个年级。

01

Tens of thousands of young people took to the streets in more than 30 German cities on Saturday, 31 October 2026.

2026 年 10 月 31 日星期六，德国 30 多个城市有数万年轻人走上街头。

02

The protests were called by “Gen Z regelt”, an initiative that came together only weeks earlier through a TikTok trend.

抗议由「Gen Z regelt」发起，这个倡议几周前才通过一个 TikTok 趋势形成。

03

Its demands include more money for schools and education, stronger climate action and measures against the rising cost of living.

其诉求包括给学校和教育更多经费、更强有力的气候行动，以及应对生活成本上涨的措施。

04

The group also rejects any return of compulsory military service and opposes more state surveillance.

该团体还拒绝恢复义务兵役，并反对扩大国家监控。

05

Most rallies stayed peaceful, but police stopped marches in Cologne, Frankfurt and Stuttgart because some participants wore masks and set off fireworks.

多数集会保持和平，但警方在科隆、法兰克福和斯图加特叫停了游行，因为一些参与者戴面罩并燃放烟火。

06

The organisers said more than 68,000 people had taken part by the evening; more than 183,000 had registered online.

组织者说，到晚上已有超过 6.8 万人参加；线上报名者超过 18.3 万。

07

Germany's national student conference distanced itself from the movement and announced its own demonstration in Berlin on 20 November.

德国全国学生会议与这场运动保持距离，并宣布 11 月 20 日在柏林自己办一场游行。

08

In Erfurt, about 1,900 people marched behind banners reading “Bilden statt Ballern” – “educate, don't shoot”.

在埃尔福特，约 1900 人举着「要教育，不要炮火」的牌子游行。

B2 B2 · 书面表达（被动、分词短语、名词化）
🎧 听这一版
01

With rallies in more than 30 cities, the newly founded initiative “Gen Z regelt” staged a nationwide youth protest on 31 October 2026.

2026 年 10 月 31 日，新成立的「Gen Z regelt」在 30 多个城市发起了一场全国性的青年抗议。

02

The movement emerged within weeks through a TikTok trend; its core team consists of about 30 young people who had met online shortly beforehand.

这场运动在几周内通过一个 TikTok 趋势形成；其核心团队由约 30 名此前不久才在网上结识的年轻人组成。

03

Its demands connect education funding, climate policy, mental health care and addiction services with relief from rising living costs, framed as a question of fairness between generations.

其诉求把教育经费、气候政策、心理治疗与成瘾援助同减轻生活成本连在一起，并以代际公平为框架。

04

The organisers explicitly reject reintroducing compulsory military service, a proposal that has regained weight in Germany's security debate.

组织者明确拒绝重新引入义务兵役——这一主张在德国的安全辩论中重新获得分量。

05

An open letter to Chancellor Friedrich Merz, signed among others by Heidi Reichinnek of the Left Party and Ricarda Lang of the Greens, gave the demands a first foothold in established politics.

一封致总理默茨的公开信让这些诉求首次在既有政治中获得立足点，联署者中有左翼党的 Heidi Reichinnek 和绿党的 Ricarda Lang。

06

While most rallies remained peaceful, police halted marches in Cologne, Frankfurt and Stuttgart over masking and pyrotechnics, and the national student conference distanced itself from the movement's opaque structures.

虽然多数集会保持和平，警方仍因蒙面与烟火在科隆、法兰克福和斯图加特叫停游行；全国学生会议也因该运动结构不透明而与其保持距离。

欧盟加收包裹费：一个箱子按类别收，不按件

🎧 听这一版
01

Since 1 November, parcels from outside the EU cost more.

从 11 月 1 日起，来自欧盟以外的包裹变贵了。

02

The EU charges 2 euros per product category.

欧盟每类商品收 2 欧。

03

Ten T-shirts in one parcel cost 2 euros, not 20.

一个包裹里十件 T 恤收 2 欧，不是 20 欧。

04

A parcel with T-shirts, hats and flip-flops costs 6 euros.

T 恤、帽子和人字拖的包裹收 6 欧。

05

There is also a customs fee of at least 3 euros.

此外还有至少 3 欧的关税。

06

Shops pay the fees, but prices will probably go up.

商家支付费用，但价格很可能上涨。

07

The EU wants fewer cheap parcels from China.

欧盟想要更少的中国廉价包裹。

B1 B1 · 完整句子，加了连接词和从句
🎧 听这一版
01

A new EU handling fee of 2 euros per product category took effect on 1 November 2026.

欧盟每类 2 欧的新处理费于 2026 年 11 月 1 日生效。

02

It applies to parcels from non-EU countries, whether or not they have a free trade agreement with the EU.

它适用于非欧盟国家的包裹——不论该国与欧盟是否有自贸协定。

03

The fee is charged per category, not per parcel or per item.

费用按类别征收，不按包裹或单件。

04

On top of it comes the flat customs fee of 3 euros per category introduced in July.

在此之上还有七月起每类 3 欧的固定关税。

05

Retailers and platforms must pay and show the fees at checkout.

零售商和平台必须支付，并在结账时列出费用。

06

Customers are likely to see higher prices, especially for cheap goods.

顾客很可能会看到价格上涨，尤其是廉价商品。

07

In 2025 about 6 billion parcels reached the EU, around 90 per cent of them from China.

2025 年约 60 亿个包裹到达欧盟，其中约九成来自中国。

B2 B2 · 书面表达（被动、分词短语、名词化）
🎧 听这一版
01

The EU's new 2-euro handling fee per product category, in force since 1 November 2026, targets the flood of parcels from third countries regardless of their value.

欧盟 2026 年 11 月 1 日生效的每类 2 欧处理费，针对的是不论价值高低涌入的第三国包裹。

02

Combined with the 3-euro flat customs fee per category introduced in July, each ordered category now costs at least 5 euros more than before.

加上七月起每类 3 欧的固定关税，每个下单类别现在至少比过去贵 5 欧。

03

Because the fee is charged per category, mixed parcels are hit harder: clothing, hats and shoes in one delivery are billed three times.

由于按类别征收，混合包裹受冲击更大：一单里有服装、帽子和鞋，就要计三次。

04

Retailers, importers and platforms are liable and must display the fees clearly during checkout.

零售商、进口商和平台负有支付义务，并须在结账时清晰列明费用。

05

Whether the costs are passed on is up to the sellers, but with thin margins in the low-price segment, higher prices are widely expected.

是否转嫁由卖家决定，但低价段毛利很薄，涨价被普遍预期。

06

Platforms such as Shein and AliExpress are expanding warehouses inside the EU, while Amazon remains largely unaffected because it ships 97 per cent of EU orders from European warehouses.

Shein、AliExpress 等平台在欧盟扩建仓库；亚马逊因 97% 的欧盟订单从欧洲仓发出，基本不受影响。

01

Tens of thousands of young people took part in demonstrations in more than 30 cities, demanding more money for education, climate action and lower rents.

数万年轻人参加了 30 多个城市的示威，要求更多教育经费、气候行动和更低房租。

02

Most rallies passed off peacefully, but Frankfurt and Cologne saw serious unrest.

大多数集会和平进行，但法兰克福和科隆出现了严重骚乱。

03

In Frankfurt, 17 shops were damaged and five were looted; more than 100 officers were injured, one of them seriously.

在法兰克福，17 家商店被损坏、5 家被洗劫；100 多名警员受伤，一人重伤。

04

Police arrested 54 people aged between 13 and 29.

警方逮捕了 54 名 13 到 29 岁的人。

05

Hesse's interior minister, Roman Poseck, said most of those arrested were German nationals, while the group as a whole was 'predominantly of migrant background'.

黑森州内政部长波泽克说，大多数被捕者是德国公民，而整个群体「以移民背景为主」。

06

That phrase describes family origin, not citizenship: many people with a migrant background hold German passports.

这个说法描述的是家庭出身，不是国籍：很多有移民背景的人持德国护照。

07

Federal interior minister Alexander Dobrindt blamed left-wing groups and 'troublemakers from the migrant community', but did not provide evidence.

联邦内政部长多布林特把责任归给左翼团体和「移民群体的闹事者」，但没有提供证据。

08

Nationwide, at least 250 people were arrested.

全德至少 250 人被捕。

01

The protests, organised under the slogan 'Gen Z regelt' ('Gen Z takes charge'), drew tens of thousands of mostly young people in more than 30 cities and remained largely peaceful.

以「Gen Z regelt」（Z 世代搞定）为口号组织的抗议，在 30 多个城市吸引了数万名以年轻人为主的参与者，总体保持和平。

02

In Frankfurt and Cologne, however, the demonstrations escalated: rioters smashed windows, looted shops and attacked emergency services with bottles and pyrotechnics.

但在法兰克福和科隆，示威升级：闹事者砸窗、洗劫商店，并用瓶子和烟火制品袭击救援人员。

03

Frankfurt police recorded 54 arrests of people aged 13 to 29, 17 damaged shops, five looted businesses and more than 100 injured officers, one of them seriously hurt.

法兰克福警方记录了 54 名 13 到 29 岁的人被捕、17 家商店被损坏、5 家被洗劫、100 多名警员受伤，其中一人重伤。

04

Hesse's interior minister, Roman Poseck, drew a distinction between citizenship and background: most of those arrested held German citizenship, he said, while the perpetrators as a group were 'predominantly of migrant background'.

黑森州内政部长波泽克区分了国籍与背景：他说大多数被捕者拥有德国国籍，而施暴群体「以移民背景为主」。

05

That term also covers German citizens whose families came from abroad, so it is not the same as nationality.

这个词也包括家庭来自国外的德国公民，因此不等同于国籍。

06

Federal interior minister Alexander Dobrindt blamed 'violent left-wing groups and troublemakers from the migrant community' without offering evidence, and no breakdown by nationality has been published.

联邦内政部长多布林特把责任归给「有暴力倾向的左翼团体和移民群体的闹事者」，却没有提供证据；也没有公布按国籍分列的统计。

🎧 听这一版
01

In several supermarkets in North Rhine-Westphalia and Lower Saxony, unknown attackers appear to have manipulated cooling systems remotely, causing temperatures to rise sharply.

在北威州和下萨克森州的多家超市，不明攻击者似乎远程操纵了制冷系统，使温度急剧上升。

02

Police are investigating a possible cyber attack; in Wetter-Volmarstein, suspicion focuses on the external maintenance company with remote access to the systems.

警方正在调查可能的网络攻击；在韦特-福尔马施泰因，怀疑集中在拥有系统远程访问权限的外部维护公司身上。

03

In Lilienthal near Bremen, display counters, cold stores and freezers failed overnight and heated up to around 30 degrees.

在不来梅附近的利林塔尔，冷藏柜台、冷藏库和冷冻柜夜间失效，升温至约 30 度。

04

The owner put the loss at goods worth more than 360,000 euros, all of which had to be discarded.

店主估计损失为价值超过 36 万欧元的商品，这些商品全部必须销毁。

05

Comparable incidents have been reported in other European countries over the past few days.

过去几天，其他欧洲国家也报告了同类事件。

06

The case highlights how networked refrigeration — efficient in normal operation — can become an entry point for attacks.

这起案件凸显出：联网的制冷设备在正常运行时很高效，却也可能成为攻击的入口。

01

On 4 November, the common ash was named Tree of the Year 2027 at a ceremony in Berlin.

11 月 4 日，欧洲白蜡树在柏林的一场仪式上被选为 2027 年度树。

02

The decision was driven by ash dieback, a disease caused by a fungus introduced from East Asia that has spread widely across Europe.

这一决定源于白蜡树枯梢病——一种由东亚传入的真菌引起、已在整个欧洲广泛扩散的疾病。

03

The species is one of the largest native deciduous trees and can reach 40 metres in height and up to 300 years in age.

该物种是最大的本土阔叶树之一，可高达 40 米、树龄可达 300 年。

04

Its wood is used for tool handles, sports equipment, furniture and parquet flooring.

它的木材被用于工具柄、运动器材、家具和镶木地板。

05

Some specimens show a degree of tolerance, but no fully resistant tree is known so far.

一些个体表现出一定耐受性，但迄今没有已知完全抗病的树。

06

Conservationists are calling for better protection of the ash and its habitat along rivers and streams.

自然保护者呼吁更好地保护白蜡树及其在河流小溪边的栖息地。

01

The Union wants Bavarian state parliament president Ilse Aigner to succeed Frank-Walter Steinmeier.

联盟党希望巴伐利亚州议会议长伊尔泽·艾格纳接替施泰因迈尔。

02

According to media reports, CDU/CSU and the SPD have already agreed on the 61-year-old, although the formal process is not complete.

据媒体报道，基民盟/基社盟与社民党已就这位 61 岁的人选达成一致，尽管正式程序尚未完成。

03

The president is chosen by the Federal Assembly, which consists of 630 Bundestag members and 630 delegates from the state parliaments.

总统由联邦大会选出，该机构由 630 名联邦议员和 630 名州议会代表组成。

04

The vote is set for 30 January 2027 in the Bundestag in Berlin.

投票定于 2027 年 1 月 30 日在柏林联邦议院举行。

05

Because Steinmeier cannot serve a third term, the seat is open in any case.

由于施泰因迈尔不能第三次连任，这个职位无论如何都会空出来。

06

If elected, Aigner would be the first woman to hold the office; the Left party has criticised the nomination as a party-political appointment.

若当选，艾格纳将是担任该职的第一位女性；左翼党批评这一提名是政党政治的分职。

The Schwarzmilzferner, the last remaining glacier in the Allgäu Alps, lost its status after an exceptionally hot summer.

阿尔高阿尔卑斯仅存的最后一座冰川在异常炎热的夏天后失去了身份。

它担心该平台对儿童和青少年的保护不够。

The recommendation system records what users watch and then plays increasingly similar videos.

06

如果不做改变，该公司可能面临高额罚款。

01

A study by the consulting firm Ernst & Young shows that the number of women on German corporate boards has reached a record high.

安永咨询公司的一项研究显示，德国公司董事会中的女性人数创下历史新高。

02

In 2025, 101 women held board positions for the entire financial year at Dax, M-Dax or S-Dax companies.

2025 年，有 101 位女性在 DAX、MDAX 或 SDAX 公司整个财年都担任董事。

03

That is more than three times the figure from 2013, when only 33 women held such posts.

这比 2013 年的 33 位增长了两倍多。

04

In the Dax alone, women now hold 50 board seats, roughly 30 percent.

仅在 DAX，女性目前占据 50 个董事席位，约占 30%。

05

The share is 28 percent in the M-Dax and 18 percent in the S-Dax.

MDAX 的比例是 28%，SDAX 是 18%。

06

Pay for male and female board members, excluding chief executives, is also converging: the gap has fallen to 26,000 euros.

不含首席执行官的男女董事薪酬也在趋同：差距已降至 2.6 万欧元。

07

The authors say smaller companies still have some catching up to do.

作者表示，较小的公司仍需追赶。

01

Cologne's carnival season opened on 11 November at 11:11 a.m. with street parties in the city centre.

科隆的狂欢季在 11 月 11 日上午 11 点 11 分以市中心的街头庆祝开场。

02

Tens of thousands of people in costumes took part, while several music groups performed on stages.

数万名穿着扮装的人参与其中，同时多个舞台上有乐队演出。

03

At one event, sign language interpreters translated the lyrics live and stood on stage with the musicians.

在一场活动中，手语翻译现场翻译歌词，并与乐手一起站在舞台上。

04

This allowed deaf and hard-of-hearing guests to follow the songs and celebrate together, and admission was free for them.

这使听障观众也能跟上歌曲、一起庆祝，而且对他们入场免费。

05

One interpreter said the work is exhausting because it demands full concentration, but the atmosphere is wonderful.

一位翻译说，这份工作很累，因为需要全神贯注，但气氛特别好。

06

The season continues until Ash Wednesday, with the Rose Monday parade on 8 February 2027 as its highlight.

这一季持续到圣灰星期三，最高潮是 2027 年 2 月 8 日的玫瑰星期一游行。

01

With the traditional opening on 11 November at 11:11 a.m., Cologne entered a new carnival season that runs until Ash Wednesday.

随着 11 月 11 日上午 11 点 11 分的传统开场，科隆进入了一个持续到圣灰星期三的新狂欢季。

02

Tens of thousands of costumed revellers filled the streets while music groups performed on stages across the city centre.

数万名盛装打扮的狂欢者挤满街道，乐队在市中心的多个舞台演出。

03

In a notably inclusive programme, sign language interpreters translated the lyrics live on stage so that deaf and hard-of-hearing guests could follow along.

在一项明显强调包容的安排中，手语翻译在舞台上现场转译歌词，让听障观众也能跟上。

04

Admission was free for those guests, and the interpreters described the work as demanding because it requires rhythm, emotion and precision at the same time.

这些观众免费入场；翻译们说这份工作很辛苦，因为要同时做到跟上节奏、传递情绪和保持准确。

05

The highlight of the season comes on Rose Monday, 8 February 2027, when the city's main parade takes place.

这一季的最高潮在 2027 年 2 月 8 日的玫瑰星期一，当天举行城市的主要游行。

06

For many people in the Rhineland, carnival is seen as a fifth season of the year.

对莱茵兰很多人来说，狂欢节被视为一年中的「第五季」。

01

On 16 November the state parliament of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern re-elected Manuela Schwesig as state premier on the first ballot.

11 月 16 日，梅前州州议会在首轮投票中再次选举曼努埃拉·施韦西希为州长。

02

She received 39 votes, one for each seat held by her coalition of the SPD, the Left party and the Greens.

她获得 39 票，正好等于其社民党、左翼党和绿党联盟所持席位数。

03

多数至少需要 36 票。29 张反对票全部来自选择党。

05

社民党掌管五个部，左翼党两个，绿党一个。

在 9 月 20 日的州选中，选择党以 38,2% 成为最强政党，而基民盟以 4,9% 未能进入议会。

07

Because no other party will work with the AfD, it is the only opposition party in the parliament.

由于没有其他党愿与选择党合作，它是议会中唯一的反对党。

社民党、左翼党与绿党的联盟是该州历史上首个三党联盟，也标志着绿党首次加入该州政府。

施韦西希没有排除竞选社民党联邦领导层的可能，但强调该州事务仍是她的首要任务。

Five EU States Plan Return Hub in Rwanda from 2027

德国等五国：2027 年在卢旺达建「遣返中心」
第 53 期 2026-11-16 nachrichtenleicht.de (Deutschlandfunk) · 2026-11-16（自主改写） A2 · B1 · B2
← 左右滑动翻页 · 挑你能读的那一版 →
🧵 相关内容及周边知识 → 01 / 05
A2 A2 · 短句为主，最常用的词
🎧 听这一版
01

Germany and four other EU countries want to build a centre for refugees in Rwanda.

德国和另外四个欧盟国家想在卢旺达为难民建一个中心。

02

The other countries are Denmark, the Netherlands, Greece and Austria.

另外几个国家是丹麦、荷兰、希腊和奥地利。

03

The centre is for people who did not get asylum in Europe.

这个中心接收的是在欧洲没有获得庇护的人。

04

These people must leave, but they cannot go back to their home countries, for example because they have no passport.

这些人必须离境，但回不了自己的国家——比如因为没有护照。

05

The plan should start in 2027.

这个计划应该从 2027 年开始。

06

At first, about 100 people are planned, around 20 from each country.

一开始计划约 100 人，每国约 20 人。

07

Many people criticise the plan. Aid groups and two German parties, the Greens and the Left, are against it.

很多人批评这个计划。援助组织和德国的两个党——绿党和左翼党——反对它。

08

They say it is not clear whether human rights are protected in Rwanda.

他们说，卢旺达的人权是否得到保障并不清楚。

09

Rwanda's interior minister has promised the people a second chance, with training and work.

卢旺达内政部长向这些人承诺第二次机会，包括培训和工作。

02 / 05
B1 B1 · 完整句子，加了连接词和从句
🎧 听这一版
01

Five EU states want to open a joint return hub in Rwanda in 2027: Germany, Denmark, the Netherlands, Greece and Austria.

五个欧盟国家想在 2027 年在卢旺达开设联合遣返中心：德国、丹麦、荷兰、希腊和奥地利。

02

The plan was presented by Germany's interior minister, Alexander Dobrindt, at a migration conference in Vienna.

该计划由德国联邦内政部长亚历山大·多布林特在维也纳的一场移民会议上介绍。

03

It targets people whose asylum cases have been finally decided and who are legally required to leave, but cannot be returned to their home countries.

它针对的是庇护程序已终局决定、有离境义务、却无法被送回原籍国的人。

04

According to media reports, families, vulnerable people and criminals are not meant to be sent there.

据媒体报道，家庭、易受伤害者和罪犯不会被送到那里。

05

About 20 places per country are planned at first, roughly 100 people in total; for Germany the figures are 40 to 50 people and about 20 million euros in the 2027 budget.

初期计划每国约 20 个名额，总共约 100 人；对德国而言是 40 至 50 人，以及 2027 年预算中约 2000 万欧元。

06

UNHCR and IOM are to be involved, and Germany's migration office is to check standards on the ground.

联合国难民署和国际移民组织将参与其中，德国联邦移民局将在当地核查标准。

07

Aid organisations, the Greens and the Left say the plan raises human rights concerns.

援助组织、绿党和左翼党表示，这个计划引发人权担忧。

08

Talks with Rwanda are the most advanced, but the practical set-up is still at an early stage.

与卢旺达的谈判走得最远，但实际筹建仍处于早期阶段。

03 / 05
B2 B2 · 书面表达（被动、分词短语、名词化）
🎧 听这一版
01

Germany, Denmark, the Netherlands, Greece and Austria plan to run a joint “return hub” in Rwanda from 2027.

德国、丹麦、荷兰、希腊和奥地利计划从 2027 年起在卢旺达共同运营一个「遣返中心」。

02

The plan was presented by Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt at a migration conference in Vienna, attended by Austria's Chancellor Stocker and Denmark's Prime Minister Frederiksen.

该计划由内政部长亚历山大·多布林特在维也纳的一场移民会议上介绍，奥地利总理施托克尔和丹麦首相弗雷泽里克森出席了会议。

03

It targets people who have completed asylum procedures and are legally obliged to leave but cannot be removed because their home countries refuse to take them back.

它针对的是走完庇护程序、依法必须离境、却因原籍国拒绝接收而无法被遣返的人。

04

Media reports say families, vulnerable persons, unaccompanied minors and criminals are to be excluded.

媒体报道称，家庭、易受伤害者、无人陪伴的未成年人和罪犯将被排除在外。

05

Initially about 20 places per state are planned; Germany is expected to take 40 to 50 people at a cost of about 20 million euros in the 2027 federal budget.

初期计划每国约 20 个名额；德国预计接收 40 至 50 人，2027 年联邦预算中约耗资 2000 万欧元。

06

UNHCR and IOM are to accompany the process, while the Federal Office for Migration (BAMF) is to monitor compliance with German standards on site.

联合国难民署和国际移民组织将陪同程序，联邦移民局将在现场监督德国标准的执行。

07

Rwanda's interior minister Vincent Biruta promised those affected a “second chance” through training and work, while human rights groups and the opposition Greens and Left warned of inadequate conditions.

卢旺达内政部长文森特·比鲁塔向当事人承诺通过培训和工作给予「第二次机会」，而人权组织以及反对党绿党和左翼党警告条件不足。

08

Dobrindt insisted the project is “not in any way comparable” to Britain's failed Rwanda scheme, which would have outsourced asylum processing.

多布林特强调，该项目与英国失败的卢旺达方案「完全不可相提并论」——后者原本要把庇护程序外包。

01

From January, all households and companies in Germany will pay less electricity tax.

从一月起，德国所有家庭和公司都将少交电力税。

02

The governing parties CDU, CSU and SPD agreed on the cut after long talks.

执政三党基民盟、基社盟和社民党在长时间商谈后就减税达成了一致。

03

一个家庭省多少取决于它用多少电。

05

三口之家每月省近 8 欧元，独居者约省 3 欧元。

06

The state will lose several billion euros a year because of the cut.

由于这次减税，国家每年将损失数十亿欧元。

07

For this reason, the lower tax is limited to one year for now.

因此，低税率暂时只实行一年。

08

It is still unclear whether the state can afford the cut in 2028.

06

Thuringia is planning a change in its schools: children with a hearing disability should be able to learn sign language as their first foreign language.

图林根州计划在学校做出改变：有听力障碍的孩子应能把手语作为第一外语来学习。

02

Normally, English is the first foreign language at schools in Thuringia.

通常，图林根的学校以英语作为第一外语。

Sign language is not spoken. Words are shown with movements of the hands and arms.

04

The mouth is also used, but almost no sound is made.

嘴也会用到，但几乎不发出声音。

对听不见或听力很差的人来说，手语是一种重要的沟通方式。

06

The new rule is still a plan, but it is expected to reach schools soon.

这将为现行规定增加一种选择——按照现行规定，该州学校通常以英语为第一外语。

这一新安排仍在筹划中，预计很快就会在学校推行。

01

The BSW missed the five-percent threshold in the 2025 federal election by a very small margin.

BSW 在 2025 年联邦选举中以极小差距未过 5% 门槛。

02

According to the official result, the party won 4.981 percent; 9,529 votes were missing.

据官方结果，该党得票 4.981%；还差 9,529 票。

03

The party believes that some ballots were counted incorrectly or confused with those of a small party with a similar name.

该党认为一些选票被错误计数，或与名称相似的小党选票混淆。

04

Germany's Federal Constitutional Court rejected the complaint as inadmissible.

德国联邦宪法法院以不合法为由驳回申诉。

05

The judges said the party did not describe specific errors in enough detail.

法官说，该党没有足够具体地说明错误。

06

A close result does not change the rules, the court added.

法院补充说，结果接近并不改变规则。

07

The BSW called the decision wrong and wants recounts whenever results are close.

01

Germany's Federal Constitutional Court has dismissed the BSW's challenge to the 2025 federal election result as inadmissible.

德国联邦宪法法院以不合法为由驳回 BSW 对 2025 年联邦选举结果的申诉。

02

With 4.981 percent of the vote, the party fell just short of the five-percent threshold required to enter parliament; 9,529 votes were missing.

该党得票 4.981%，以微弱差距未达进入议会所需的 5% 门槛；还差 9,529 票。

03

The court found the complaint insufficiently substantiated, noting that general suspicions do not prove an election error that could have changed the result.

法院认定申诉理由不充分，指出笼统的怀疑不能证明可能改变结果的选举错误。

04

The party had argued that ballots were confused with those of a similarly named group and that some votes were overlooked or wrongly invalidated.

该党主张，选票与一个名称相似的团体混淆，一些票被漏计或被错误判无效。

05

The BSW called the ruling a miscarriage of justice, while the conservative Union proposed reforming the election-review process.

BSW 称裁决是司法误判，保守派联盟则提议改革选举审查程序。

The National Read-Aloud Day took place for the 23rd time on 20 November 2026.

01

From December, people in Germany can buy Flixtrain tickets from Deutsche Bahn.

从 12 月起，德国人可以在德铁那里买 Flixtrain 车票。

They can book on the website or in the DB app.

他们可以在网站或德铁 App 上订票。

03

A trip can use one train from Deutsche Bahn and one from Flixtrain.

一次行程可以坐一趟德铁、一趟 Flixtrain。

04

But people still get two separate tickets.

但人们仍然会拿到两张分开的票。

05

If the first train is late, travellers may miss the second one.

如果第一趟车晚点，旅客可能会错过第二趟。

06

Then they often have to buy a new ticket.

那样他们往往得买一张新票。

Deutsche Bahn gets money for every Flixtrain ticket it sells.

德铁每卖出一张 Flixtrain 票就能拿到钱。

🎧 听这一版
01

Deutsche Bahn and the private company Flixtrain have agreed to work together on ticket sales.

德铁和私营公司 Flixtrain 已同意在售票上合作。

02

Flixtrain tickets will be available on bahn.de and in the DB Navigator from 7 December.

从 12 月 7 日起，Flixtrain 车票将在 bahn.de 和 DB Navigator 上出售。

03

They are valid for journeys that start on 13 December.

它们适用于 12 月 13 日起的行程。

04

Customers can combine both companies in one booking, but they receive two separate contracts.

乘客可以在一次预订中组合两家公司，但会拿到两份分开的合同。

05

If a delay causes a missed connection, passenger rights apply only to each separate ticket.

如果晚点导致错过衔接，乘客权益只适用于各自的车票。

06

In most cases, travellers then need to buy a new ticket.

大多数情况下，旅客这时需要买一张新票。

07

The deal is voluntary; there is no law forcing the two companies to cooperate yet.

这项协议是自愿的；目前还没有法律强制两家公司合作。

🎧 听这一版
01

The cooperation is a sales agreement, not a single through-ticket: each leg is covered by its own transport contract.

这项合作是一份销售协议，而不是一张通票：每一段都由各自的运输合同覆盖。

02

This becomes a problem when a delayed Deutsche Bahn train makes passengers miss their Flixtrain connection.

当德铁列车晚点使乘客错过 Flixtrain 衔接车时，这就成了问题。

03

In that case, compensation and rebooking rights apply only within the contract that was broken.

在这种情况下，赔偿和改签权利只适用于被违约的那份合同。

04

Pressure for the opening came from competition authorities and the European Commission, which wants dominant rail operators to sell rivals' tickets.

开放的压力来自竞争监管机构和欧盟委员会，后者希望占主导地位的铁路运营商代售竞争对手的车票。

05

Deutsche Bahn receives a sales commission for each Flixtrain ticket sold through its channels.

德铁通过其渠道每卖出一张 Flixtrain 票，就获得一笔销售佣金。

06

Consumer groups welcome the step but call for full passenger rights across providers.

消费者团体欢迎这一步，但呼吁各运营商之间提供完整的乘客权益。

01

Germany will launch the digital driving licence in mid-December, a few weeks later than planned.

德国将在 12 月中旬推出数字驾照，比原计划晚几周。

02

The licence is stored in the i-Kfz-App, which is run by the Federal Motor Transport Authority.

驾照存放在由联邦机动车运输管理局运营的 i-Kfz-App 里。

03

Inside Germany, the digital version counts as proof of a driving licence at police checks.

在德国境内，数字版本在警察检查时可作为驾照证明。

04

For the time being, drivers must also carry their ID card, because the photo has not yet been added to the app.

目前司机还必须随身带身份证，因为照片还没有加入 App。

05

The digital licence is not recognised abroad; the plastic card remains mandatory at the border.

数字驾照在国外不被承认；在边境仍必须使用塑料卡片。

06

The EU plans a digital licence that works across Europe by 2030.

欧盟计划到 2030 年推出全欧洲通用的数字驾照。

07

Using the app is voluntary.

使用这个 App 是自愿的。

01

The launch was originally scheduled for the end of November but was delayed because the technical connection to the vehicle registers took longer than expected.

上线原定于 11 月底，但因与车辆登记系统的技术对接耗时超出预期而推迟。

02

The digital licence initially serves only as proof of the driving licence within Germany.

数字驾照起初只作为德国境内的驾照证明。

03

Because the photo cannot yet be transferred, drivers must be able to prove their identity with an ID card during the transition period.

由于照片尚不能转入，过渡期内司机必须能用身份证证明身份。

04

Outside Germany the digital version has no legal standing, so the physical card is still required.

在德国以外，数字版本没有法律效力，因此仍需实体卡。

05

To use the service, drivers need an ID card with the online ID function and an NFC-capable smartphone.

要使用这项服务，司机需要带在线身份功能的身份证和支持 NFC 的智能手机。

06

The move is part of a broader but cautious digitalisation of German administration.

这一步是德国行政更广泛而谨慎的数字化进程的一部分。

01

A court in Cologne has decided that the Catholic Church must pay 550,000 euros to a woman.

科隆的一家法院裁定，天主教会必须向一位女性支付 55 万欧元。

02

The woman is 60 years old now.

这位女性现在 60 岁。

03

As a child, she was the foster daughter of a Catholic priest.

她小时候是一名天主教神父的养女。

04

The priest abused her for many years, about 50 years ago.

那名神父在约 50 年前多年对她实施性侵。

05

In 2022 the priest was sentenced to twelve years in prison.

2022 年，那名神父被判处 12 年监禁。

06

This is the highest amount the Catholic Church in Germany has ever paid to a victim.

这是德国天主教会迄今向受害人支付的最高金额。

07

The woman had asked for at least 830,000 euros.

这位女性曾要求至少 83 万欧元。

08

The court said that amount was too high.

法院说这个金额过高。

B1 B1 · 完整句子，加了连接词和从句
🎧 听这一版
01

The Higher Regional Court in Cologne has ordered the Archdiocese of Cologne to pay 550,000 euros in compensation to a woman who was abused as a child.

科隆高等法院判令科隆总教区向一位儿时遭到性侵的女性支付 55 万欧元赔偿。

02

The woman, now 60, was the foster daughter of a Catholic priest and was abused over many years around 50 years ago.

这位如今 60 岁的女性曾是一名天主教神父的养女，约 50 年前多年遭到性侵。

03

The priest was sentenced to twelve years in prison in 2022.

那名神父于 2022 年被判处 12 年监禁。

04

It is the highest sum the Catholic Church in Germany has ever paid to a victim of abuse; the previous record was 300,000 euros.

这是德国天主教会迄今向性侵受害人支付的最高金额；此前的纪录是 30 万欧元。

05

A lower court had first dismissed the case, saying the priest had acted more or less as a private person.

一家下级法院最初驳回了诉讼，称那名神父「或多或少是以私人身份」行事。

06

The higher court disagreed and ruled that the priest had used his position in the church to win the woman's trust.

高等法院不同意这一判断，裁定那名神父利用自己在教会中的职位取得了这位女性的信任。

07

For that reason, the court held the church partly responsible for his actions.

因此，法院认定教会对其行为负有共同责任。

08

The woman had demanded at least 830,000 euros, but the court considered this too high.

这位女性曾要求至少 83 万欧元，但法院认为这个金额过高。

09

Of the 550,000 euros, 360,000 euros had already been paid, so the archdiocese still owes 190,000 euros.

在这 55 万欧元中已支付 36 万欧元，因此总教区仍欠 19 万欧元。

03 / 05
B2 B2 · 书面表达（被动、分词短语、名词化）
🎧 听这一版
01

With its ruling, the Higher Regional Court of Cologne has confirmed that the Catholic Church can be held liable for sexual abuse committed by one of its priests.

通过这一判决，科隆高等法院确认，天主教会要对其神父所实施的性侵承担责任。

02

The woman, now 60, had been abused over many years in the 1970s and 1980s while living as the foster daughter of a priest.

这位如今 60 岁的女性，在 1970 至 1980 年代作为神父的养女多年遭到性侵。

03

The priest, sentenced to twelve years in prison in 2022, had used his position in the church to gain the girl's trust; most of the abuse took place in the parish house.

那名于 2022 年被判处 12 年监禁的神父，利用自己在教会中的职位取得了女孩的信任；大部分侵害发生在教区住宅里。

04

The lower court had dismissed the claim on the grounds that the man had acted as a private individual, but the higher court affirmed the archdiocese's liability for acts committed in an official capacity.

下级法院曾以该男子以私人身份行事为由驳回诉讼，但高等法院确认了总教区对职务行为的责任。

05

The award of 550,000 euros is the highest the Catholic Church in Germany has ever paid to a victim of abuse, surpassing the previous maximum of 300,000 euros.

判给的 55 万欧元是德国天主教会迄今向性侵受害人支付的最高金额，超过了此前 30 万欧元的最高额。

06

Because 360,000 euros had already been paid through an independent recognition commission, the archdiocese still owes 190,000 euros.

由于已有 36 万欧元通过一个独立认定委员会支付，总教区仍欠 19 万欧元。

07

The plaintiff had demanded at least 830,000 euros; the court considered this excessive and set the amount lower.

原告曾要求至少 83 万欧元；法院认为这一诉求过高，把金额定得更低。

A man from Lithuania tried to row across the Pacific Ocean alone.

02

His name is Aurimas Mockus. He is 44 years old.

He started in October from San Diego, in the United States.

他的小船严重损坏，他在海上等了三天。

07

He sent an emergency signal. A rescue team heard it.

他发出求救信号，一支救援队收到了。

08

On 3 March, an Australian navy ship rescued him.

3 月 3 日，一艘澳大利亚海军舰艇把他救了起来。

09

He is safe now. The ship is taking him to Sydney.

他现在安全了。船正把他送往悉尼。

10

Only a few people have rowed across the Pacific alone.

只有极少数人独自划过太平洋。

01

A rower from Lithuania has been rescued by an Australian navy ship after he ran into a storm near Australia.

一名来自立陶宛的划船者在澳大利亚附近遭遇风暴后，被一艘澳大利亚海军舰艇救起。

02

The man, Aurimas Mockus, is 44 years old. He started his trip alone in October from San Diego, in the United States.

这名男子 Aurimas Mockus 今年 44 岁。他十月独自一人从美国圣迭戈出发。

03

He wanted to row about 12,000 kilometres to Brisbane, Australia. He was only 740 kilometres from the coast when he hit a tropical cyclone.

他想划大约 12000 公里到澳大利亚布里斯班。遭遇热带气旋时，他离海岸只有 740 公里。

04

His small boat was badly damaged, and he stayed in the sea for three days before the rescue.

他的小船严重损坏，在被救之前他在海上待了三天。

05

He sent an emergency signal, and a rescue team made radio contact with him. He told them he was very tired.

他发出求救信号，救援队与他建立了无线电联系。他告诉他们自己非常疲惫。

06

On 3 March, he was brought onto the Australian warship. The ship is now taking him to Sydney.

3 月 3 日，他被接到澳大利亚军舰上。这艘船现在正送他前往悉尼。

07

Mockus wanted to be one of the few people who have rowed across the Pacific alone and without stopping.

Mockus 想成为极少数独自、不间断划过太平洋的人之一。

08

做到这一点的人很少，其中包括 1983 年的英国人 Peter Bird 和 2023 年的澳大利亚人 Michelle Lee。

🎧 听这一版
01

A rower attempting a solo crossing of the Pacific Ocean has been rescued by an Australian navy vessel after his boat was severely damaged in a tropical cyclone.

一名试图独自横渡太平洋的划船者，在船被热带气旋严重损毁后，被一艘澳大利亚海军舰艇救起。

02

Aurimas Mockus, 44, set off from San Diego in California in October, hoping to row roughly 12,000 kilometres to Brisbane on Australia's east coast.

44 岁的 Aurimas Mockus 十月从加州圣迭戈出发，目标是划大约 12000 公里，抵达澳大利亚东海岸的布里斯班。

03

He had come within 740 kilometres of the mainland when he encountered Cyclone Alfred, whose winds reached 80 kilometres per hour.

遭遇气旋 Alfred 时，他距离大陆仅剩 740 公里；当时风速达到每小时 80 公里。

04

Stranded in the Coral Sea for three days, Mockus activated an emergency beacon, which allowed rescuers to establish radio contact. He was described as fatigued.

Mockus 在珊瑚海被困三天，他启动了应急信标，救援人员因此得以建立无线电联系。他被描述为「极度疲惫」。

05

The enclosed vessel he had been travelling in was largely destroyed, and he was able to recover only a few personal belongings.

他乘坐的封闭式小艇大部分被毁，他只抢回了少数随身物品。

06

He was taken aboard a Royal Australian Navy warship on 3 March and is being transported to Sydney.

3 月 3 日他被接上澳大利亚皇家海军军舰，目前正被送往悉尼。

07

Solo, non-stop crossings of the Pacific remain exceptionally rare.

独自、不间断横渡太平洋仍然极为罕见。

08

Peter Bird of Britain became the first to attempt one in 1983, although he was towed for the final 48 kilometres. Australia's Michelle Lee became the first woman to complete the crossing in 2023.

1983 年英国人 Peter Bird 首次尝试，尽管最后 48 公里是被拖行的。2023 年澳大利亚人 Michelle Lee 成为首位完成横渡的女性。
